issues.description: The solution repository defines animal constructors that accept (String name, int age) (Animal, Seal, Pig, Goat), while the problem statement and the provided template/main expect single-argument constructors (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")) and the instructions state constructors should initialize the class attributes (the UML shows only a name attribute). This constructor parameter mismatch will confuse students and break the example usage in the template Main and the intended UML: students will implement single-argument constructors per the spec but the solution uses two-argument constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align constructors across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to provide single-argument constructors that accept only the name (matching the UML and template Main), removing the extra age parameter, or (B) update the problem statement/template to document and use an age attribute so constructors consistently take (String name, int age). Prefer option A to match the UML in the problem statement and the example Main.

issues.description: The problem UML and description specify that Animal has a single attribute 'name: String', but the solution's Animal class declares an additional 'age' attribute (private int age). This attribute mismatch diverges from the UML/specification and may confuse students about the required fields and constructor responsibilities.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the Animal class matches the UML: remove the extraneous 'age' attribute from the solution (and adjust constructors and getters/setters accordingly), or update the problem statement/UML to include 'age' as a required attribute and reflect that in the template Main and instructions. Prefer removing 'age' in the solution to match the current UML and template usage.

issues.description: Constructor/attribute mismatch for Animal and its subclasses: the problem statement and the template Main examples imply animals are constructed with a single String name (and the UML lists only a 'name' attribute), but the solution introduces an additional 'age' attribute on Animal and implements constructors taking (String name, int age) in Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat. This breaks the conceptual mapping (and the provided Main usage) because students expect to call single-argument constructors and to initialize only the 'name' attribute as described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor and attribute definitions consistent across artifacts. Either (A) remove the extra 'age' attribute and change Animal (and Seal, Pig, Goat) constructors in the solution to take only String name (matching the UML/problem statement and the template Main usage), or (B) update the problem statement and the template Main examples to document and use a two-parameter constructor (String name, int age) and explicitly mention the new 'age' attribute so all artifacts match.
